comments.body: If I just install `ghostty` do I get the service files installed? If not, we need to change this PR so that they are, but allow people to opt out of the service file install.

I apologize for the distraction. After digging deeper, my issue is mostly with the way Home Manager manages the things. After forking and overriding the home-manager module for ghostty I was able to rewrite these configs without this PR patch in place.

Again, sorry for the time burden, but today I learned a lot more about how overlays and package builds and the whole system works..... versus the black magic approach I used before.

reviews.body:
I think so. I don't run NixOS, but all the files are installed into the nix store by default. In home-manager, the default behavior is they get linked into the environment (i.e. as a systemd user service). The difference is, with this patch, I can override all the of the various service files. I tried without it, but then I get configuration conflicts.

Whether I override the files or not, they get installed into the nix store. Here's the find output (truncated for readability):

```shell
find /nix/store/syf466iq87anh9sv88jbm49l47qfj8xb-ghostty-1.2.3/ \
  -name app-com.mitchellh.ghostty.service -o \
  -name com.mitchellh.ghostty.metainfo.xml -o \
  -name  com.mitchellh.ghostty.desktop -o \
  -name com.mitchellh.ghostty.service
.../share/metainfo/com.mitchellh.ghostty.metainfo.xml
.../share/kio/servicemenus/com.mitchellh.ghostty.desktop
.../share/applications/com.mitchellh.ghostty.desktop
.../share/systemd/user/app-com.mitchellh.ghostty.service
.../share/dbus-1/services/com.mitchellh.ghostty.service
```

I don't see a need to merge this

These new outputs aren't "Nixpkgs conventions" that I've ever really seen around. I also don't know how they would help with "modularity" - splitting the service will still pull in the main bin output, for example

I'm also sure there are other ways to make the binary use NixGL? I'm honestly not too sure how this would even help with it either
